description: Raise n=512 panel occupancy past 3 CTAs/SM now that the barrier-optimized panel_factor_kernel_512 changed the kernel's resource profile. A sibling found n=512 B=640 runs at 3 CTAs/SM, capped by the panel's SMEM footprint P=(m+1)*cb; the barrier-shortening (brief 37) may have changed register/SMEM usage. Profile the new panel_factor_kernel_512's ncu Block-Limit-SMEM / Block-Limit-Registers / achieved-occupancy, then SHRINK whichever caps it — reduce the resident SMEM panel (the cb-wide reduction scratch, the T-factor tile, or stream fewer rows) and/or register pressure — to fit 4 CTAs/SM. At B=640 (640 matrices, 148 SMs) more CTAs/SM = more co-resident matrices = better latency hiding of the serial panel chain (the inter-CTA hiding brief 26 showed is what makes n=512 fast). FP32 panel. Keep n!=512 as parent (19ebe6249). MEASURE absolute nsys panel-kernel-time (throttle-stable) + ncu achieved-occupancy before/after. No 'stream' substring; all guards CLEAN.

Tighten panel_factor_kernel_512 SMEM to exact (LB,IB,cb) needs: drop DEAD wsh(32f), size red=IB*nwarps (was MAXCB*16=512f), normscratch=MAXWARPS, T-region=cb*(cb+1). Frees 2.94KB resident SMEM (77.12->74.18KB at j=0). ncu n512: j=0 panel SMEM-limited 2->3 CTAs/SM (theoretical occ 12.5->18.75%, achieved 11.0->13.42%, warps/SM 7.05->8.59); j=0 ncu duration 656->471us (-28%); first-6-panels ncu sum 2744.9->2548.6us (-7.2%, clock-locked). Registers 95->96 (Block Limit Reg 5, non-binding). All guards CLEAN, n512 factor_rtol=0.00122. Geomean 8142us under contention (parent logged 12150 under contention; not directly comparable). j=0 still SMEM-capped at 3 (need <57KB for 4); P=(m+1)*cb dominates -> next attack P.

n=512 cb=16 sweep on tight-SMEM low-barrier kernel. P=(m+1)*16~32KB at j=0 -> 5-6 CTAs/SM (more co-resident matrices). REGRESSION: n=512 dense shape3 17327->21806us (+26%), mixed 20927->22326, rankdef 17154->21636, clustered 17329->21804; non-n512 shapes unchanged. Geomean 8142->8665us (worse). DECISIVE: raising CTAs/SM by shrinking cb does NOT pay at n=512 -- 32 panels vs 16 doubles panel+trailing-GEMM round-trips and the fused w_c trailing pass scales with cb; latency-bound panel can't use the extra occupancy enough to overcome round-trip cost. cb=32 stays optimal. Validates CLEAN.

n=512 cb=24 sweep: P=(m+1)*24~49KB at j=0 -> exactly 4 CTAs/SM (the brief's target tier). n=512 dense shape3 17327(cb=32)->17933us (+3.5%), mixed 20927->21099, rankdef 17154->17752, clustered 17329->17931; non-n512 unchanged. Geomean 8142->8242us (slightly worse). Sweep is MONOTONIC: cb=32(3 CTAs/SM,17327)<cb=24(4 CTAs/SM,17933)<cb=16(5-6,21806). REACHING 4 CTAs/SM does NOT beat the per-CTA round-trip cost (~22 panels of 24 vs 16 of 32). cb=32 at 3 CTAs/SM stays optimal. Validates CLEAN.

Brief step-3 minblocks sweep: __launch_bounds__(LB, minblocks) made a template param, _MINB_512=4 forces the compiler to target 4 CTAs/SM. ncu n512: NO-OP -- registers stay 96/thread (Block Limit Reg=5 unchanged), Block Limit Shared Mem=3 unchanged, achieved occ 13.42% identical, j=0 duration 471us identical to minblocks=1. Geomean 8164us (= trial-1 8142 within noise); n=512 dense 17334 (= 17327). DEFINITIVE: SMEM (74KB/CTA) is the HARD occupancy limiter -- 4*74KB=296KB > 228KB B200 cap, so minblocks cannot place a 4th CTA; registers were never the limiter so minblocks has nothing to trade. The ONLY path to >3 CTAs/SM at cb=32 is fewer resident rows (P=65.7KB at j=0 is the wall). Validates CLEAN.

ROW-WINDOWED panel: caches only the top WR=384 rows of the n=512 panel in SMEM (resident P 65.7KB->49.3KB at j=0 -> fits 4 CTAs/SM at cb=32), rows [384,m) read/written in-place from global H. ~150-line index-surgery rewrite; validates CLEAN, n=512 factor_rtol=0.00122 BIT-IDENTICAL to fully-resident. REGRESSION ~2x: n=512 dense 17327->33208us (+92%), mixed 20921->33352, rankdef 17159->32586, clustered 17328->32894; geomean 8142->12463us. The brief's 'keep fewer rows resident' lever DOES reach 4 CTAs/SM but is strongly net-negative: the global tail traffic (bottom 128 rows re-read/written, strided through row-major H, every micro-panel ~cb times) dwarfs the latency-hiding from the extra co-resident CTA. Confirms brief-35's n=1024 finding ALSO holds at n=512 B=640 despite the abundant CTA count -- the panel is work/latency-bound, not occupancy-bound, past 3 CTAs/SM. Net: 3 CTAs/SM at cb=32 (trial-1 tight-SMEM) is the occupancy optimum; every path to 4 (narrower cb, row-windowing) loses.

KEEPER: _RS_512=0 routes n=512 to the trial-1 tight-SMEM fully-resident panel (3 CTAs/SM at j=0). Geomean 8152us = trial-1 8142 (noise); n=512 dense 17333, mixed 20923, rankdef 17165, clustered 17332; non-n512 byte-identical to parent. All guards CLEAN. nsys: panel 79.8% of n=512 capture, 11.69ms/16-panels (= trial-1). This is the brief's net result -- the ONLY occupancy win that pays at n=512 is the FREE scratch trim (j=0 2->3 CTAs/SM, no work added); reaching 4+ CTAs/SM via narrower cb (trials 2-3) or row-windowing (trial 5) both work but lose to the work/traffic cost. The panel is work/latency-bound past 3 CTAs/SM.

Brief 45 (n=512 panel occupancy past 3 CTAs/SM) -- KEEPER 180169e89 (geomean 8152us under contention = parent-class; n=512 dense 17333us). STEP-1 LIMITER (ncu, n512 dense): SMEM is the SOLE binding occupancy limiter -- Block Limit Shared Mem caps the panel (j=0 = 2 CTAs/SM on the parent, 3 after my trim), while Block Limit Registers=5 (95-96 reg/thread) and Block Limit Warps=16 are both NON-binding. P=(m+1)*cb=65.7KB at j=0 dominates the footprint; the 6 panels run at SMEM 77/73/69/65/61/57KB -> 2/3/3/3/3/4 CTAs/SM. STEP-2 WIN (KEEPER, trial 1 d9874b30): tightened the panel SMEM to the exact (LB,IB,cb) instantiation -- dropped the DEAD wsh buffer, sized red=IB*nwarps (was MAXCB*16=512f), T-region=cb*(cb+1) -- freeing 2.94KB (77.12->74.18KB), which lifts j=0 from 2->3 CTAs/SM with ZERO work added: j=0 panel ncu duration 656->471us (-28%), first-6-panels clock-locked sum 2744.9->2548.6us (-7.2%), nsys panel-total stable (<0.01% across 3 captures). This is the FREE occupancy win the brief targeted. STEP-3 (reach 4 CTAs/SM) -- THREE measured routes, ALL net-negative: (a) minblocks=4 template (trial 4) is a NO-OP -- SMEM 74KB hard-caps at 3 (4*74=296KB>228KB), registers unchanged 96, occupancy identical; confirms registers were never the limiter; (b) cb sweep (trials 2-3) -- cb=24 ncu-CONFIRMED reaches 4 CTAs/SM (achieved occ 13.4->20.1%) but n=512 dense +3.5%, cb=16 reaches 5-6 CTAs/SM but +26%; monotonic cb=32(3)<cb=24(4)<cb=16(6); (c) ROW-WINDOWING (trial 5, ~150-line correct rewrite, WR=384 resident rows + tail in-place in global H, validates BIT-IDENTICAL) reaches 4 CTAs/SM but +92% (~2x) -- global tail traffic dwarfs the gain, matching brief-35's n=1024 result. CONCLUSION I MEASURED: 3 CTAs/SM at cb=32 is the occupancy optimum; the panel is WORK/LATENCY-bound, not occupancy-bound, past 3 CTAs/SM -- so shrinking P (the only path to 4+) costs more work/traffic than the extra co-resident CTA hides. OPENINGS the manager may pursue: (1) the keeper's clean -7.2% panel win is NOT yet in the recorded global best -- it should fold cleanly (n!=512 byte-identical to parent); a clean-GPU re-benchmark would register it. (2) The j=0 panel (m=512, the single most expensive at 471us / 2 of 16 panels) is the only one still below 3 CTAs/SM tier-wise on the parent -- a STRUCTURAL departure that shrinks P WITHOUT adding traffic (e.g. a coalesced contiguous tail-staging buffer instead of strided in-place H, or processing j=0 as a cooperative 2-CTA split a la the cluster panel but for the SM-saturated case) is untested and could capture the j=0 tier without the row-windowing traffic penalty. (3) warp-cycles-per-issued stayed ~6.4 (top stall is serial-recurrence, not barriers/SMEM) -- the panel's floor may now be the serial column-recurrence latency, not occupancy, pointing follow-ups at the recurrence (look-ahead within the micro-panel, brief 43's angle) rather than more occupancy. Left in tree (OFF): the row-windowed kernel + minblocks template (both measured, both neutral/negative, _RS_512=0/_MINB_512=1).
